title: Bit flip preserves the other coordinates
statement: Let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ be a point of the Boolean hypercube, and let $i,j$ be coordinate indices with $i\ne j$. Writing $x^i$ for the point obtained from $x$ by flipping the $i$-th coordinate, we have $(x^i)_j = x_j$; that is, flipping coordinate $i$ leaves coordinate $j$ unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: x is a point of the Boolean hypercube {0,1}^n
i and j are coordinate indices
replaced:
If $i\ne j$ then flipping coordinate $i$ does not change coordinate $j$:
$(x^i)_j = x_j$.
